questions.q: What does a 3-way match add to the checks performed by a 2-way match?
options: A credit check on the customer
A comparison against the actual quantity received in the Receiving system
A tax recalculation
An inspection record
questions.explain: 3-way matching adds the receipt — the quantity actually received — to the price and quantity-ordered checks already performed in a 2-way match.

questions.q: Why could a PO configured for 2-way matching never produce a Qty Rec hold?
options: 2-way matching never looks at the receiving record at all
Qty Rec holds are disabled by default
2-way matching only applies to service invoices
Qty Rec holds only exist in 4-way matching
questions.explain: A 2-way match compares only the PO and invoice (price and quantity ordered); it never references receiving data, so a receipt-based hold cannot be triggered.

questions.q: In the Harbor & Vance Logistics ticket, what was actually wrong?
options: The invoice overbilled for units never shipped
The PO quantity ordered was entered incorrectly
The supplier's price was outdated
The receiving record was incomplete — only part of the shipment had been logged as received
questions.explain: The supplier shipped all 500 units, but the warehouse had only recorded a partial receipt of 320 units; the invoice itself was accurate.

questions.q: What was the correct fix for the Qty Rec hold in this ticket?
options: Manually release the hold since the vendor was asking about payment
Reduce the invoice quantity to match what was recorded as received
Enter the missing receipt for the remaining units, dated to their actual arrival
Change the PO's matching level to 2-way
questions.explain: Since the invoice was correct and the receiving record was incomplete, the fix was to enter the missing receipt rather than alter the invoice or override the hold.

questions.q: What general lesson does this ticket share with Lesson 5's Price hold ticket?
options: Both holds should always be manually released
A matching hold involves multiple documents (PO, receipt, invoice), and you must determine which one is actually inaccurate before fixing it
Matching holds are always caused by the supplier
Only the invoice can ever be the cause of a matching hold
questions.explain: In both tickets, the key step was identifying which specific document was actually wrong — the PO in Lesson 5, the receipt here — rather than assuming the invoice was always at fault.
